findings.title: A rotation member HWiNFO no longer lists is counted as rotating, shown as a raw hex key, and called missing only in a tooltip
findings.area: Sensor Dial > Reading > Rotation (chips, note, summary, status block)
findings.state_task_viewport: dial-configured overridden to readingKey gpu, rotationKeys [gpu, f0099999:0:1000000, hot] (on-dial reading live, one member gone); also dial-missing after 'Pick another reading'. Task: understand what the dial will rotate through and recover. 373x410.
findings.observed: MEASURED (probe2 P2): status block empty; header state 'Live · Shared Memory'; the member chip's visible text is 'f0099999:0:1000000' with a dashed amber border; the word missing exists only in its title ('Not in the current HWiNFO layout; keeps its place and shows as missing') and an sr-only span; note 'Rotation moves through these 3 readings only, in this order.'; Reading summary 'GPU Temperature · rotation: 3 readings'. MEASURED (J6): in dial-missing, after re-picking the on-dial reading the status block clears, the dead chip stays, and the note says 'these 2 readings' with only one live.
findings.evidence: READ: runtime skips keys the snapshot lacks (src/rotation.ts:16-26 pickedReadings, 43-50), so the dial actually moves through 2 readings, not 3. Chip markup ui/pi-common.js:410-448 (missing = class + sr-only + title only); note ui/pi-common.js:682-691 counts stored keys. Shot: %TEMP%\hw-r3-beginner\p2\P2-missing-member.png, j\J6-4-dial-missing-repicked-full.png.
findings.affected_user: beginner; everyone sighted (screen reader users hear the sr-only note)
findings.correction: Give a missing chip a visible pill in the same style as 'on dial' (for example 'not in HWiNFO') instead of tooltip-only state, and count only live members in the note while naming the rest: 'Rotation moves through these 2 readings; 1 not listed by HWiNFO is skipped until it returns.'
findings.tradeoff: An extra pill can wrap the chip row at 373 px; the count now changes when a sensor sleeps, and the note speaks on the 'rotation' live channel, so a dropout may be announced.
findings.acceptance_test: With the P2 override at 373x410: the missing chip's visible text (sr-only excluded) contains a word meaning missing; the note's number equals the live member count (2); opening the panel writes nothing.

findings.title: One click on the bare '×' beside a group name deletes the group, its name and its readings, with no confirm and no undo
findings.area: Sensor Dial > Rotation groups (group header remove control)
findings.state_task_viewport: dial-groups, task: tidy or rename a group, 373x410
findings.observed: MEASURED (probe4): the control is a '×' glyph, 28x28, 4 px right of the group name field; its meaning is title/aria-label only ('Remove this group (its readings leave the rotation)'). One click: 2 writes; groups CPU:2, GPU:2 become GPU:2; rotationKeys 4 -> 2; the name 'CPU' is gone; only visible feedback is the note turning into 'One group only: it acts as a plain rotation set until you add a second.'; no undo control exists. INFERRED (walkthrough): a '×' at the end of a text field is the common 'clear this field' affordance, so a beginner wanting to clear a name can destroy the group.
findings.evidence: READ: ui/pi-common.js:640-646 (glyph, title, aria-label), handler 3980-3995 (immediate splice + writeRotation). Precedent for a two-step destructive action in this codebase: Replace shared settings arms on the first click and asks again (ui/pi-common.js:4228-4262).
findings.correction: Reuse the Replace pattern: the first click arms and the control reads 'Remove group and its 2 readings?' for 5 s; a second click removes. The resting glyph can stay '×' if space demands, but the armed state is text.
findings.tradeoff: One extra click for power users; the armed state needs a timeout, a reset on blur/rebuild and a polite announcement.
findings.acceptance_test: On dial-groups: one click on .hw-group-remove[data-group="0"] writes nothing and shows visible text naming the consequence; a second click within 5 s writes once and removes the group; waiting 5 s disarms with no write.

findings.title: At 200% zoom the header text column collapses to single letters; at 160 px the header alone is taller than the panel
findings.area: Pinned header (all sensor panels), narrow widths
findings.state_task_viewport: key-empty at 160x410 and 189x410; dial-configured and key-missing at 189x410. Task: read what the panel is and find the reading search.
findings.observed: MEASURED (probe2 P9): 160x410: header 428 px (unpinned via data-pin-off), 'Sensor Reading key' stacks one letter per line, the first screen holds only the header, reading search at y=702. 189x410: header 200 px, 'Sens / or / Reading / key' breaks mid-word, search at y=474 (dial 442, key-missing 679). No horizontal overflow. Outside my core role; listed because the brief names these viewports (dedupe with the low-vision reviewer).
findings.evidence: READ: .hw-head is a non-wrapping flex row (ui/pi.css:87-93); key face flex:none 72 px; .hw-head-text flex:1 1 160px, min-width:0 with overflow-wrap:anywhere (pi.css:154-161); the max-width:199px block only shrinks the fold buttons (pi.css:225-238). Shots p2\P9-key-empty-160.png, P9-key-empty-189.png. WCAG 1.4.10 Reflow is defined at 320 CSS px, so no standards failure is claimed.
findings.correction: Under 200 px let the header wrap (flex-wrap: wrap inside the existing max-width:199px block) so the text takes a full-width row under the face.
findings.tradeoff: The dial CSS comment says the face always sits beside its text; this changes that only under 200 px. The header stays unpinned there (already the case).
findings.acceptance_test: At 160x410 and 189x410: #head-kind renders on one line, no word breaks inside 'Sensor', and the header is at most 220 px tall.

findings.title: Opened reading lists land mostly or entirely below the 410 px panel's fold
findings.area: Reading search (key and dial), dial rotation checklist
findings.state_task_viewport: Fresh key-empty, dial-empty, dial-configured at 373x410 (and 320x560 for comparison). Task: browse for a first reading; add readings to a rotation.
findings.observed: MEASURED (probe2 P3): clicking the key's reading search opens the overlay list at y 301-529: 2 rows fully visible (109 of 228 px). Dial 'On the dial now': 2 rows (93 px). At 320x560 the same lists show 8 rows. MEASURED (P1): the rotation search sits at y 393-421, half on screen; clicking its visible part opens the inline checklist at y 427-585: 0 px visible; focus lands in the search and nothing else changes on screen. The density tool marks the rotation search 'first screen' (top 393 < 410), which hides this. INFERRED: browsing is a first-timer's natural move when names like 'Tctl/Tdie' are unknown.
findings.evidence: READ: openList never scrolls the page (ui/pi-common.js:2493-2508); the detail collector already scrolls on open (onOpenChange, pi-common.js:2819-2833). Shots j\J1-1-list-open.png, p2\P1-dial-configured-rotation-search-click.png.
findings.correction: On open (never while typing or on echoes), if the list's bottom is below the viewport, scroll the page by the overflow, capped so the search stays just under the pinned header (reuse the collector's overlap arithmetic).
findings.tradeoff: The page moves on focus, including for a keyboard user tabbing in; must not fight the 'Pick another reading' reveal, which already centers the search.
findings.acceptance_test: At 373x410: clicking #picker-search on key-empty leaves at least 6 fully visible rows; clicking the visible part of #pickerr-search on dial-configured leaves at least 4 visible rows with the search still below the pinned header; no writes.

findings.title: The reading put on the dial first is silently left behind by the next turn when it is not ticked into a new rotation
findings.state_task_viewport: dial-empty: pick GPU Temperature, then tick GPU Hot Spot Temperature and GPU Power in the rotation search. 373x410.
findings.observed: MEASURED (J2): writes rotationKeys [hot, power], readingKey unchanged; chips 'GPU Hot Spot Temperature' (white ring: auto-selected first member) and 'GPU Power'; no chip says 'on dial'; note 'Rotation moves through these 2 readings only, in this order.'; summary 'GPU Temperature · rotation: 2 readings'. The checklist row shows 'on dial' unticked only while the list is open. INFERRED (walkthrough): a beginner expects the reading they just put on the dial to belong to the rotation they are building, and the only highlighted chip (the ring on Hot Spot) can read as 'current'.
findings.evidence: READ: with a set, a turn from a key not in it enters at the first member and never returns (src/rotation.ts:63-72 stepReading, 43-50). Membership write ui/pi-common.js:338-359; selection fallback 394-404. Shot j\J2-2-after-ticks-full.png.
findings.correction: When a set exists and the on-dial reading is not a member, add one line to the note: 'GPU Temperature (on the dial now) is not in this rotation; the next turn moves to GPU Hot Spot Temperature.' No auto-add (that would be an unasked write).
findings.tradeoff: One more line in the dial's longest fieldset; it must follow turns and echoes.
findings.acceptance_test: After the J2 steps, the rotation block's visible text names the on-dial reading as not in the rotation and names the first member; ticking GPU Temperature removes the line; no extra writes.

findings.title: On a Legacy dial (the default) the visible groups note promises groups will work; the correction sits below the fold after a long paragraph
findings.observed: MEASURED (J5b): visible note '2 groups. They take effect once two of them hold readings; until then rotation runs as one flat list.'; the Legacy caveat (#groups-preset-help) is 46 px below the viewport, after the five-line #rotation-help paragraph. Once both groups fill, the note becomes 'Rotation needs two or more readings in a group to move inside it', which also implies groups work.
findings.evidence: READ: without a group-switch gesture groups never take effect (src/ui/dial-overview.ts:25-30, src/controls.ts:135-144); note text ui/pi-common.js:719-729 ignores presetCanSwitchGroups; markup order ui/sensor-dial.html:68-71. Shots j\J5b-split.png, j\J5b-crop.png.
findings.correction: Make the note preset-aware ('2 groups, but these gestures cannot switch groups, so rotation runs through all of them as one list.') and move #groups-preset-help directly after the note, before #rotation-help, with a reveal button to #f-preset like the theme band's 'Change'.
findings.tradeoff: Note logic depends on the preset (already tracked as presetCanSwitchGroups); a Custom gesture change must re-render the note.
findings.acceptance_test: On dial-configured after Split at 373x410, text saying these gestures cannot switch groups is inside the viewport and the note no longer says 'They take effect once two of them hold readings'; switching Gestures to Elite removes the caveat.

findings.title: 'Reload sensor list' and 'Retry now' give no acknowledgement when the problem persists
findings.area: Status block recovery actions (key and dial)
findings.state_task_viewport: key-missing (Reload sensor list) and key-unavailable (Retry now), 373x410
findings.observed: MEASURED (J6): after a click the status text is byte-identical, focus stays on the button, the picker placeholder never changes, nothing is announced; the requests do go out (getSensorTree, getPreview); 0 writes. A beginner cannot tell 'checked, still missing' from 'the button did nothing'.
findings.evidence: READ: renderStatus returns early when its signature is unchanged (ui/pi-shell.js:623-625); retry handler ui/pi-shell.js:653-667.
findings.correction: After a retry whose answer keeps the same problem, add one line inside the existing status region, for example 'Checked again just now: still not in HWiNFO's list.' (or 'still no HWiNFO data'), dropped when the problem changes.
findings.tradeoff: One more line in the status block; it must stay signature-based so ticks never re-announce it.
findings.acceptance_test: On key-missing, click Reload sensor list: within 1.5 s the status text differs and contains 'again'; the live region fires once; no writes; a second click still produces a perceivable change.

findings.title: Guidance that is true only in some states is shown in all of them
findings.area: Sensor Dial > Reading help lines and rotation notes
findings.state_task_viewport: dial-configured with rotationDisabled true; dial-configured with Custom turn = Cycle stat; dial-missing; dial-empty; dial-unavailable. 373x410.
findings.observed: MEASURED (probe4, J6, J2, captures): 'Turning the dial changes this too.' stays under 'On the dial now' while the Controls summary says 'Legacy: turns ignored ...' or 'Custom: turn cycles the stat ...', and while the on-dial reading is missing (the face says 'reselect in settings'). 'Empty: rotation moves through all readings of the picked sensor.' shows on dial-empty with nothing picked. 'Select one in the list below, then Earlier and Later set their order.' and 'Split into groups' show with an empty rotation.
findings.evidence: READ: turns are no-ops with Ignore turns or a pin (src/actions/sensor-dial.ts:346-350) and with a missing current reading (sensor-dial.ts:521-526); with nothing picked a turn walks the whole snapshot (src/rotation.ts:52-57). Copy: ui/sensor-dial.html:55, :66; ui/pi-common.js:685.
findings.correction: Derive the lines from state: the turn help from preview.effective.controls plus rotationDisabled and missing ('Turns are ignored on this dial; see Controls.'); the empty note with no pick: 'Empty: the first turn picks a reading, then rotation moves through that reading's sensor.'; hide the ordering sentence until the set has a member.
findings.tradeoff: Help text that changes with settings; each variant is one line, so layout shift stays small.
findings.acceptance_test: With rotationDisabled true, #picker-help's visible text no longer says turning changes it; on dial-empty the rotation note does not mention a picked sensor; the ordering sentence is absent while #rotation-set has no option.

findings.title: The folded Controls summary never mentions the pressed turn, which is Elite's group switch

findings.evidence: READ: dialInteractionSummary builds turn, push, tap and cycle only (ui/pi-model.js:195-210).
findings.correction: Add 'pressed turn <gesture>' to the summary when it differs from the turn.
findings.tradeoff: The summary wraps to three lines at 373 px; exact strings in test/pi-model.test.ts:148-154 change.
findings.acceptance_test: On dial-groups the Controls summary contains 'pressed turn switches sensor or group'; on Legacy it is unchanged.

findings.title: Split into groups (and by the same code path Merge and group remove) opens the rotation checklist as a side effect
findings.state_task_viewport: dial-configured, click or Enter on 'Split into groups'. 373x410.
findings.observed: MEASURED (probe3): before, #pickerr-list hidden; after Split (pointer and keyboard alike) it is visible, 158 px with 37 rows, while focus sits in 'Name of group 2'; scrolling up shows an open checklist nobody opened (p2\P3b-after-split-up.png). A 158 px layout shift happens above the focus.
findings.evidence: READ: the rebuild's focus fallback focuses #pickerr-search when the pressed action button no longer exists (ui/pi-common.js:576-589); focus opens the list (2529-2532); the handler then moves focus into the rotation block, which counts as inside the picker (alsoWithin), so the focusin closer keeps it open (2879-2889, 4005-4026). Merge and group remove take the same fallback (READ, not run).
findings.correction: Let the fallback focus the search without opening it, or skip the fallback when the action handler places focus itself.
findings.tradeoff: None known beyond the focus path in rotationFocusRestore.
findings.acceptance_test: After Split, Merge and group remove on dial-configured/dial-groups, #pickerr-list.hidden is true and #pickerr-search has no aria-expanded="true".

findings.title: 'Sensor' and 'source' each mean two different things across the panel and faces
findings.area: Copy across key face, dial face, Reading, Rotation, Controls, Press, Connection
findings.state_task_viewport: All sensor panels; walkthrough of key-empty, dial-empty, dial-groups, key-details copy
findings.observed: READ (copy): key face 'Pick a sensor / in settings' and 'Sensor missing / pick again' (src/ui/state-screens.ts:46,50), dial face 'Sensor missing / waiting' (src/actions/sensor-dial.ts:1041), while the panel calls the same thing a 'reading'. Elsewhere 'sensor' means HWiNFO's hardware group: 'all readings of the picked sensor' (ui/pi-common.js:685), 'Switch sensor or group' (ui/sensor-dial.html:246), 'this sensor's readings' (ui/pi-model.js:104). 'Source' is the hardware group in 'this sensor's source' (pi-model.js:190), 'Every reading from this reading's source' (ui/sensor-reading.html:267) and the header's second line, and the data provider in 'Data source', 'Auto source', 'Reopening HWiNFO's source'. MEASURED: the HTML placeholder 'Search readings or sources' is replaced by 'Search readings' at runtime (pi-common.js:2294), so a first-timer is never told sources are searchable. INFERRED: 'Pressed turn: switches sensor or group' can be read as 'the next reading'.
findings.evidence: Greps of the frozen ui/ copy and src/ui/state-screens.ts; J1 firstScreen pickerPlaceholder 'Search readings'.
findings.correction: Panel copy first (cheap): 'reading' for one value, 'sensor' for HWiNFO's group (HWiNFO's own word), 'data source' only for Shared Memory and Gadget; change 'this sensor's source' and 'this reading's source' to 'sensor'; keep the placeholder 'Search readings or sensors'. Change face text only if the owner accepts the test cost.
findings.tradeoff: 'Sensor missing' is pinned in about 15 unit and e2e assertions (test/back-face.test.ts, test/detail-faces.test.ts, scripts/e2e-*.mjs) and docs screenshots; test/pi-model.test.ts:69,144 pin two summary strings.
findings.acceptance_test: A grep of visible panel copy finds 'source' only next to data source/Shared Memory/Gadget and never uses 'sensor' for a single reading; the reading search placeholder mentions sensors.

findings.title: The group radio that decides where new ticks land has no visible label; its explanation is about 280 px below it
findings.state_task_viewport: dial-groups, task: add a reading to a chosen group. 373x410.
findings.observed: MEASURED (J5): the radios' meaning is in title and aria-label only ('New ticks go to group 1 (CPU)'); 'Ticks land in the group marked by the radio' sits at y 756-836 while the first radio is near y 472. The search label does name the target ('Readings for CPU', 'Readings for GPU' after the radio) and the tick lands there.
findings.correction: While groups exist, swap the first sentence of #pickerr-help for 'Ticks go to the group with the filled circle; they never change what is on the dial now.'
findings.acceptance_test: On dial-groups, the sentence tying ticks to the radio renders within 120 px of the first radio.

findings.title: While the pointer rests on a theme chip, the Theme line names that chip instead of the selection, and the resolved Default disappears
findings.state_task_viewport: key-configured with Default checked; hover Graphite or Midnight. 373x410 (DPR 2 crop).
findings.observed: MEASURED (J3, probe2 P4): the line reads 'Theme Midnight' while the Default chip keeps its ring and aria-checked=true; '· Void' is gone until the pointer leaves; 0 writes. INFERRED: the preview mattered when chips were unnamed swatches; every chip now carries its name, so the line can keep answering 'what is selected and what Default draws'.
findings.evidence: READ: renderThemeLine shows previewTheme ?? themeOverride (ui/pi-common.js:3485-3499, 3576-3592). The e2e contract asserts the focus preview (scripts/e2e-pi-panels.mjs:440-444). Shot p2\P4-hover-midnight@2x.png.
findings.correction: Keep the line on the selection (with '· Void' for Default); if a preview is kept, append it after the selection ('Default · Void, pointing at Midnight').
findings.tradeoff: Breaks the e2e check 'focus on a swatch names it without picking it', which the integrator must update.

findings.title: With no theme in the shared settings, the band and Shared defaults disagree about what Default draws
findings.area: Theme band vs Advanced > Shared defaults
findings.state_task_viewport: key-configured opened with globals {theme: ember}, then with globals lacking theme (the state a Replace shared settings without a theme field leaves). 373x410.
findings.observed: MEASURED in the simulator (probe2 P5): band 'Default · Ember'; Shared defaults select 'Void'; Shared defaults summary 'Void · theme text · accents by type · decimal data units'.
findings.evidence: READ: the plugin keeps its current deck theme when the stored one is absent or invalid (src/ui/theme-store.ts:80-83); the select shows data-default="void" (ui/sensor-reading.html:330); the summary assumes void (ui/pi-model.js:250-252); the band uses effectiveDeckTheme (ui/pi-common.js:3473-3475).
findings.correction: Have the Shared defaults select and summary show the resolved deck theme (effectiveDeckTheme from the themes payload) when globals.theme is absent or unknown.
findings.tradeoff: The select would display a value that is not stored; it must still write nothing until changed.
findings.acceptance_test: In the P5 state, the band, the shared select and the shared summary all name Ember; opening writes nothing.

findings.title: The dial header names the reading differently from the face when a rotation name is set
findings.observed: MEASURED (capture, J7 run): header 'GPU Hot Spot Temperature'; chip 'Hot Spot' with 'on dial'; face row 'HOT SPOT'.
findings.evidence: READ: face title precedence is label, then rotation name, then HWiNFO label (src/actions/sensor-dial.ts:1089-1091); the header skips the rotation name (ui/pi-shell.js:528-534).
findings.correction: Treat the rotation name like a custom label in the header: name on line 1, HWiNFO label and sensor on line 2.
findings.tradeoff: The header must resolve aliases the way the dial does.
findings.acceptance_test: On dial-groups, #head-reading equals 'Hot Spot' and #head-source starts with 'GPU Hot Spot Temperature'.

findings.title: With HWiNFO off, a key or dial without its own label cannot say which reading it holds
findings.area: Header and reading search in the unavailable state
findings.observed: MEASURED (J6): header 'Saved reading'; search placeholder 'Saved reading kept (no HWiNFO data to show it)'; no place in the panel names the reading. INFERRED: with several keys, a beginner cannot tell which is which until HWiNFO runs.
findings.evidence: READ: names come only from the live tree (ui/pi-shell.js:413-424); stored names are deliberately avoided (ui/pi-common.js:122-131).
findings.correction: If the plugin saw the reading earlier in this session, let it answer with the last-seen label from memory only (like the fold memory), shown as 'CPU (Tctl/Tdie) (last seen)'.
findings.tradeoff: Touches the plugin protocol; must never be written to settings; a label can be stale.
findings.acceptance_test: After the reading was live once in the session, the unavailable header names it with a 'last seen' marker; after a plugin restart it says 'Saved reading' again.

keep_unchanged: First reading on an empty key (MEASURED J1, J1b): search on the first screen at 373x410 (y 271-299, 4 Tabs per density T1); typing then Enter, or one row click, writes exactly one field (readingKey); header, face, state line ('Live · Shared Memory') and theme help update at once.
Enter with no typed filter never commits the unrelated top row (READ ui/pi-common.js:2602-2611).

The header state line answers 'is the data available and live' before and after a pick: 'HWiNFO ready · Shared Memory', 'Live · Shared Memory', 'Not updating for 42 s', 'No HWiNFO data', 'Saved reading not found' (MEASURED).

Groups: the rotation search label names the receiving group ('Readings for CPU') and follows the radio; a tick lands in that group (MEASURED J5).
'Ticking adds a reading; it never changes what is on the dial now.' is accurate (READ pi-common.js:338-359).
Layout hint when Two readings is chosen before reading 2 is picked, plus the matching Reading summary (MEASURED P8).
The Controls section's 'What the dial does now' list with its caveats (Ignore turns, auto cycle off) (MEASURED J7).
'Title after a turn: Clears (default)' states what the runtime does (READ src/actions/sensor-dial.ts:559-566).
